papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. In 500M-parameter LLaMA compression at a 4% validation-loss distortion budget, it reports 1.89× compression versus 1.14× after standard weight decay.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether spectral regularization improves low-rank compressibility while preserving model quality.

evidence.quote: For the 500 500 M model and a 4 % 4\% distortion budget, it supports 1.89 × 1.89\times compression, compared with 1.14 × 1.14\times after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: ORCA applies temporary orthogonality regularization early in training, then removes it. The inspected LLaMA results report lower final validation loss than Muon at 350M and 1.3B after 100B tokens.
papers.relevance: Tests how the timing of spectral regularization affects effective rank and LLM training quality.

evidence.quote: Compared with Muon, ORCA reduces the final loss by 0.0194 0.0194 at 350M and 0.0244 0.0244 at 1.3B, with consistent gains at both scales.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Spectrally Targeted Muon selectively orthogonalizes momentum singular directions. Its NanoGPT analysis separates changes in weight spectra from changes in validation loss.
papers.relevance: Useful for studying which singular directions matter to Muon and whether effective rank tracks model quality.

evidence.quote: Note that structure and performance don’t move together: AdamW collapses rank and still performs well, the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss, and full-spectrum updates keep the spectrum flat for free.

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Proposes a LoRA-specific Riemannian preconditioner. On eight commonsense-reasoning datasets, the inspected LLaMA2-7B results report mean accuracy of 82.34 versus 81.68 for unpreconditioned AdamW LoRA.
papers.relevance: Combines LoRA optimization geometry with measured language-model fine-tuning behavior.

evidence.quote: Table 3: Top-1 test accuracy in LoRA fine-tuning for the LLaMA2-7B model on the eight commonsense reasoning datasets with different preconditioning.

papers.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Shows that trace-norm-regularized adaptation can have low-rank global minimizers controlled by a frozen-feature bottleneck. Its stationary-point result requires a generic positive-semidefinite perturbation and does not rule out spurious local minima.
papers.relevance: Provides a theoretical account of LoRA rank and its relationship to nuclear-norm regularization and factor weight decay.

evidence.quote: Trace-norm regularization then selects a low-rank representative among all matrices that induce the same observed output.
This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem; Proposition 4.9 gives an explicit limitation.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon trains structured weights with blockwise Muon updates. Quality runs compare it with Monarch-AdamW at 257M and 1B MoE scale; separate 6.89B systems measurements report lower peak memory and step time than dense Muon.
papers.relevance: Measures model-quality, memory, and speed tradeoffs of structured, matrix-aware LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: In quality runs, Monarch–Muon improves over Monarch–AdamW at fixed structure: 3.06 vs. 3.09 in the dense 257M model and 2.68 vs. 2.77 in the 1B MoE model
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: ResQAdam retains a BF16 momentum and uses low-rank adaptive coordinates plus a residual sign update for quantization-aware training. Across three tested LLMs, inspected hardware results show 71.3%–73.2% less optimizer-state memory than AdamW and under 2% lower throughput.
papers.relevance: Directly informs the quality, peak-memory, and throughput tradeoffs of low-rank optimizer-state compression, albeit in QAT.

evidence.quote: The training throughput decreases by less than 2% compared to standard AdamW in all evaluated cases.

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: PMRC adds an orthogonal residual correction to memory-efficient subspace optimization. Its C4 pretraining comparison spans LLaMA-style models from 60M to 1.3B parameters against AdamW, Muon, GaLore, GoLore, Fira, and GUM.
papers.relevance: Closely matches low-rank-gradient pretraining and the question of whether discarded subspace residuals harm quality.

evidence.quote: We compare our multi-stage PMRC with AdamW ( Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019 ) , Muon ( Jordan et al., 2024 ) , the AdamW-based GaLore ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) , GoLore ( He et al., 2025 ) and Fira ( Chen et al., 2025a ) , and the Muon-based GUM ( Pan et al., 2025a ) .
PMRC consistently achieves the lowest training and validation losses among memory-efficient methods.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

papers.summary: Idea2Prior separates broad paper screening from bounded evidence inspection and joint ranking. Its reported historical Hit@5 is 16/30, versus 13/30 for ChatGPT web Deep Research and 11/30 for Gemini web Deep Research, with documented protocol limitations.
papers.relevance: Directly informs an auditable, application-controlled research-digest retrieval pipeline.

evidence.quote: Joint ranking combines an abstract-level shortlist with bounded, explicitly partial PDF evidence, while a retrieval-only mode avoids report-specific work.
The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

papers.summary: MapHub scores daily arXiv submissions against participant portfolios. In a small blind-rating test, its top 10% contained about 70% of raters’ highest-interest 5%, versus about 33% for a TF-IDF baseline.
papers.relevance: Offers a directly relevant design and evaluation example for personalized paper ranking in a digest.

evidence.quote: MapHub’s top 5% of papers hold about a third of it, and its top 10% about 70%, against 33% for a term-frequency baseline
MapHub is still under development, and the test is small.

papers.title: MapHub: Daily Relevance Heatmaps of New arXiv Preprints for a Research Community

limitations: The supplied evidence consists of abstracts and selected HTML passages, not independent replications or complete paper reviews.
PMRC’s exact validation-loss values and end-to-end throughput were not recovered by the repeated lexical inspections, so no numerical quality or speed claim is made for it.
Monarch-Muon’s 6.89B measurements are systems benchmarks separate from its complete quality runs; projection-refresh timings are excluded from its reported step-time comparison.
ResQAdam’s reported efficiency results concern quantization-aware training, not general BF16 pretraining.
MapHub’s relevance evaluation is small and drawn chiefly from astro-ph; transfer to this user’s LLM digest is untested.
No code repositories were independently checked, and X analysis was disabled.
